title: The lost son (Kern ch. 4)
hook: a son who ran away returns as a poor laborer; his rich father slowly raises him until he can tell him the truth

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sariputra, who feared he'd been left out, was told by name that he would become a Buddha. Your line: he too will wake.

This time the Buddha isn't the one telling the story. In chapter four of the Lotus, the disciples stand up. They've just watched Sariputra receive his promise, and they're amazed, because they had stopped expecting anything more. Subhuti and Kasyapa are among them. They bow and say: let us tell you a story, to show what has happened to us. And the story is about a runaway.
screen: `THE DISCIPLES STAND UP.` → `LET US TELL YOU A STORY.` → `A STORY ABOUT A RUNAWAY.`

segments.voice: In Kern's telling, a young man leaves his father and wanders to other lands, growing poorer. Meanwhile his father searches for him, settles in a city, and grows very rich, with storehouses, servants and a crowd at his door. All the while he thinks of his son and tells no one. One day the son, now a beggar looking for work, drifts to his father's house. He sees a great man on a throne, surrounded by attendants, and doesn't recognize him. This must be a king, he thinks. If I stay, they'll seize me and force me to work. He runs. The father knows him at once and sends servants after him, and the son is so terrified he faints. So the father has water sprinkled on his face and lets him go, saying nothing. The father sends two men who look as poor as the son to offer him a job clearing away the dirt heap, for good wages. The son takes it. The father takes off his fine clothes and jewels, puts on dirty work clothes, picks up a basket, and works beside him. He talks to him, tells him to stay, raises his wages, starts calling him son. Even so, the son still thinks of himself as a hired hand. In time the father gives him charge of the whole household and its treasure, and still the son lives in his small hut. At last, near the end of his life, the father calls together his relatives, the king and the townspeople, and announces: this is my son, who ran away long ago. Everything I have is his. The father had the truth the whole time. What he waited for was a son who could hear it without running.
screen: `A RUNAWAY GROWS POOR.` · `HE SEES A KING, AND RUNS.` · `THE FATHER IN WORK CLOTHES.` · `THIS IS MY SON.` · then, large: `THE LOST SON.`

segments.voice: Who isn't ready yet? A child, a coworker, a parent learning a phone, maybe you, learning something hard. Think of the father setting down his jewels and picking up a basket, and let one small picture come of working beside this person instead of above them.
The lost son. The disciples' parable in chapter four: a runaway too frightened to know his father, raised step by step until the truth can be told. Today's word.
Your line: the lost son. Tomorrow, the disciples say who he is. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: The parable of the lost son, told by the senior disciples in chapter four of the Lotus Sutra, is retold in East Asian Buddhist teaching as a picture of the Buddha's patient skillful means.

original.note: Sanskrit: inclination, disposition, trusting resolve; the name of chapter four in Kern's Sanskrit text.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about a rich family reunion.
what it means: the disciples see themselves in the son, raised step by step by a patient father until they can hear the whole truth.
what a scholar hears: chapter four is named for adhimukti, disposition, because the father fits each step to what the son can accept, the upaya of chapter two in a family story.

chat.says: In the Lotus story of the lost son, why doesn't the father just tell him the truth?
options: The son was too frightened to hear it, so the father worked beside him until he was ready.
The father wanted to punish him first for running away, so he made him work.
The father didn't recognize him at first, and only found out at the very end.
chat.meaning: When the son ran in terror, the father let him go and raised him step by step, telling the truth once he could hear it.

Kern.meaning: the scholar whose English translation of the Lotus this path follows

Subhuti.meaning: the elder who questions the Buddha in the Diamond Sutra

Kasyapa.meaning: one of the Buddha's great disciples

notes: Chapter 4 parable paraphrased from Kern (SBE XXI, 1884); nothing quoted.

Check: the tellers (Kern names Subhuti, Maha-Katyayana, Maha-Kasyapa and Maha-Maudgalyayana; only Subhuti and Kasyapa named here); the son's flight and fainting; the water sprinkled on his face; two poor-looking messengers; the dirt-heap job; the father in dirty clothes; the hut; the announcement before relatives and the king. Kern gives the son's years away and other figures; omitted under the claims rule.
The practice and teach avoid any comparison with the Gospel parable of the prodigal son; editor should keep it that way.
